messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-2026-44401 — hosted-inference: 503 spike (error rate >5% for 1m). Primary on-call: @mike paged. Secondary: @sarah will be next if unacked.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: INC-2026-44401 created, urgency: high. Escalation policy: hosted-inference-prod. Timeline: primary -> 2m -> secondary -> 3m -> manager.

mike: on it, looking at the SLO dashboard. starting with ingress LB and autoscaler.

jordan: seeing a burst of 502/503 from front-door in eu-west-1, maybe a misrouted model pool?

emily: confirmed latency spike correlates with model shards hitting OOM on a subset of nodes. logs: ``ERROR: kv cache miss -> OOM while allocating 1.2GB``

mike: acked. switching to incident bridge now. creating a temporary bridge: https://meet.redwood/bridges/4440123456

incidentbot: PagerDuty: INC-2026-44401 acknowledged by mike. Next escalation timer paused.

sarah: (automated) My phone is in scheduled DND until 09:30, will not respond to push. If escalation reaches me, please ping manager.

jordan: oh — PD shows secondary is silenced (DND). If primary loses connectivity, escalation will jump to manager per policy. Heads up.

emily: we have noisy retries from the model router causing cascading load. I can roll back router config to previous commit to reduce fanout. Thoughts?

mike: yes do that, but I need to keep the bridge open and confirm customer impact first.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: Escalation timer resumed (primary ack cleared after 7m). Secondary (sarah) is set to "Do Not Disturb" — next step: manager-alex.

manager-alex: pinged by PD. I'm joining the bridge. what's the customer impact?

mike: current impact: ~8% of requests returning 503 for hosted-inference customers in eu-west-1. Traffic routed to fallback models for some tenants, but larger customers with pinned versions see degraded throughput. No data exfiltration.

emily: rolling back router config now (deploy id: rollconv-2026-09-01-16:04). command: ``kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-router -n serving --to-revision=123``.

oncall-sre: FYI, I just bumped the autoscaler max pods by +20% for eu-west-1 to buy time. Not a permanent fix.

mike: thanks. after rollback, error rate dropped to 2.1% within ~90s. tracing shows fewer cross-shard KV evictions.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: Manager escalation to manager-alex fired (no ack from secondary).

manager-alex: joined. good rollback. pls monitor for 15m. also need post-incident writeup + PD policy tweak: detect DND on secondary and page backup on-call earlier.

sarah: (later) Sorry, missed the page — phone was DND. i'll sync on postmortem and we can adjust my schedule/PD rules.

jordan: recap for bridge: root cause was router config change that increased cross-shard traffic which triggered OOMs on model workers -> cascading retries -> autoscaler churn. Mitigation: rollback + scale bump + temporary cache TTL increase.

emily: pushing config to increase KV cache TTL to reduce churn. ``PATCH /configs/router { "kv_ttl": 120 }``.

mike: closing the PD incident in 10m if metrics stable. any customer-facing comms needed?

manager-alex: yes, send a short status note to affected customers (status.redwood.ai) noting transient errors in eu-west-1, root cause, and remediation steps. No action required from customers.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: INC-2026-44401 resolved by mike. Duration: 18m.

mike: resolved. thanks team. action items: 1) follow-up postmortem, 2) PD policy adjust for DND secondaries, 3) add canary for router change that simulates cross-shard load.

incidentbot: :white_check_mark: Incident closed. Please add notes to the incident tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INC-44401

sarah: will add notes and sync times to avoid future DND blindspots.

emily: I'll draft the postmortem with timeline and proposed mitigations.

jordan: adding runbook tweak to prevent autoscaler thrash during config rollouts.

oncall-sre: thumbs up. also recommend an automated check to detect when secondary is DND and add an alternate on-call target to the escalation chain.

manager-alex: thanks everyone, great quick work. follow-ups in the writeup. :thumbsup:
